## Natural history notes

A native perennial wildflower in the iris family, characterized by narrow, grass-like leaves and small, star-shaped blue to violet flowers with bright yellow centers. Despite its common name, Jeweled Blue-eyed Grass is not a true grass. It occurs primarily in dry, sandy habitats such as scrub, sandhill, and other open fire-maintained uplands, where it is adapted to full sun and nutrient-poor soils. Flowering is most conspicuous in early to mid-spring. The species is native mainly to Florida and Georgia and is considered imperiled in South Florida because of its relatively restricted distribution and dependence on intact sandy upland habitats.
